statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 86% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the weekend venue halt.
recommendation: Tail rests at a closed-market floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole horizon. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the window and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints all fall outside it: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME reopen, roughly twenty-one hours after the final published hour, where the firmer September rate path and accumulated US-Iran developments would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar that same day. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and subsequent assessment cycles will score the reopen once a live price path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed the payroll week at 29,544.15 after an orderly two-way session; with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC the full 24-hour horizon is a halted venue and Tail is published at a closed-market floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday's August payroll session at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.32 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday, so no live price path exists for NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD at this assessment, and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen roughly twenty-one hours after the final published hour. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so the first full US cash session follows on 8 September. The index outperformed a weaker tape, with the S&P 500 down 0.38% to 7,718.41, the Dow down 0.51% to 53,413.60 and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.29% to 26,506.99, while the semiconductor complex closed 3.4% higher against five of eight tracked megacaps lower, TSLA down 5.92% and AAPL down 2.51% against MU up 6.10%, AMD up 4.69% and INTC up 4.51%. Sector breadth carried the same rotation signature, with Technology up 0.77% while Communication Services fell 0.92% and Consumer Cyclical fell 1.06%. That dispersion is a rotation signature rather than the aligned single-direction stack that would justify a raised Tail. Volatility confirmed the orderly reading, with VIX closing at 14.53, up 1.47%, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. The August employment report, reverified this cycle at the BLS, printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against roughly 55,000 expected, with 55,000 of upward revisions across June and July, unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% over the year. Rate transmission stayed contained rather than disorderly: the H.15 release still shows 3 September as its latest official column, at 4.34% for the 2-year and 4.77% for the 10-year, and September hike pricing ended the week at 58.4% against 49.4% a day earlier, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC confirmed on the Federal Reserve's own calendar with a Summary of Economic Projections. The communications blackout for that meeting begins at 00:00 Eastern on Saturday 5 September, inside this horizon, which removes official commentary as a weekend catalyst. Energy remains the live geopolitical channel: WTI settled at $91.48, up 0.20%, and Brent at $92.68, up 0.8%, for weekly gains of nearly 10% and 7.6%, the steepest since mid-July, as US-Iran hostilities continued in the seventh month of the conflict with Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption unresolved. The shared cross-asset context file was healthy and 58 minutes old at this assessment and was used as delayed supporting context only; it confirmed the same rotation picture, with all seven tracked semiconductors higher by a mean 2.91% against a megacap mean of -1.22%, and every material figure above was taken from primary sources fetched this cycle. With the venue halted for the entire horizon, Tail is published at a closed-market floor of 5%, while Stress at 38% represents unpriced weekend exposure to active Middle East escalation and a firmer September rate path rather than any observed drawdown.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span the calm pre-payroll regime, the August employment release, its decay into the Friday cash close and the first hours of the weekend halt. Tail sat at 13-14% through the Asian hours and drifted to 17% into the European session while Stress climbed steadily from 52% to 62% ahead of the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw conditions took over on the 162,000 payroll surprise. Price discovery then proved orderly: the initial move was retraced, Tail fell to 20% and 18% over the following two hours and back into the low teens through the US afternoon, with dominant mode moving from event/whipsaw to mixed as semiconductor strength offset megacap weakness. The final five hours step down to a 5% closed-market floor with Stress at 38% once futures settled at 21:00 UTC. The published series remained EA_ON and green for 22 of the 24 hours, with WATCH and yellow only in the two hours immediately around the release.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly twenty-one hours after this horizon ends, and Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. Because no venue quotes during any published hour, the pathological price path that Tail measures cannot form, so forecast Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-market floor and the dominant mode of normal denotes a halted rather than a directional regime. Stress starts at 38% and drifts to 46% across Saturday and into Sunday to reflect weekend information accumulating unpriced against active US-Iran hostilities and a firmer September rate path; that exposure is real for anything carried through the break but is expressed as a single reopen gap rather than as a tradable path. The Federal Reserve communications blackout ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC begins at 00:00 Eastern on 5 September, inside the horizon, freezing the official rate-path channel for the remainder of the window and leaving geopolitical reporting as the only live weekend catalyst. Confidence decays from 86% to 72% purely with distance from the verified Friday evidence cutoff, since coverage itself is complete and was reverified this cycle against index, volatility, yield, energy and payroll primary sources. No macro release falls inside the horizon; the next verified checkpoints are the 8 September NY Fed inflation expectations and 3-year auction, PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, each at 12:30 UTC.
